title: Race condition in PIN unlock flow using queueMicrotask
reasoning: The PinGate component calls onUnlock via queueMicrotask on every render when pin.unlocked is true. This creates a race where onUnlock can be queued multiple times if React re-renders before the parent processes the first unlock. The pattern should either use useEffect with dependency on pin.unlocked, or the parent should gate re-renders defensively. The current implementation is fragile and may cause duplicate state updates in the parent.
reproduction:
1. Enter correct PIN
2. Force a re-render (e.g., theme change, window resize)
3. onUnlock queues again even though already unlocked
4. Parent may process setUnlocked(true) multiple times
recommendation: Replace the conditional queueMicrotask with useEffect: `useEffect(() => { if (pin.unlocked) onUnlock() }, [pin.unlocked, onUnlock])`. This ensures the callback fires exactly once when unlocked transitions to true.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests are included in the feature. This timing bug would require integration tests that simulate re-renders during the unlock transition.
suggestedRegressionTest: Mount PinGate with a mock onUnlock, enter the correct PIN, force a re-render, and assert onUnlock was called exactly once.
